propinquabant: propinquō, -āre, -āvī (+ dat.) — to draw near, approach (3rd pl. impf.)
propinquat: propinquō, -āre, -āvī (+ dat.) — to draw near, approach (3rd sg. pres.)
propius: propius (adv.) — nearer, more closely (compar. of prope)
pugna: pugna, -ae (f.) — fight, battle (abl. sg.; also nom. sg.)
pulsus: pellō, pellere, pepulī, pulsum — to drive, drive out, strike (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (f. nom. sg.: quae sententia) · also interrog. adj., n. nom. pl. (quae sint ea nūmina) · also exclam. adj., n. acc. pl. (quae bella exhausta canebat!; quae … regna) · also interrog. pron./adj., n. acc. pl., what? (quae quibus anteferam; quae … maiora) · also f. nom. pl. (quae … acies)
qualis: quālis, -e — of what sort; such as, like, as (m./f. nom. sg.)
quam: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. acc. sg.); quam (adv.), how; than · prius… quam (conj.), before, until · indef. after sī/nē, any, some (f. acc. sg.: si quam) · also interrog. adj., what? which? (f. acc. sg.: quam arcem?) · also tam … quam, as … as (adv./conj.) · also quam multa … sic, as many as … so · also ante … quam, before (conj., antequam split: non ante … quam)
quando: quandō (conj.) — since; (adv.) when · also indef. adv. after sī, ever (sī quandō, if ever)
quicumque: quīcumque, quaecumque, quodcumque — whoever, whatever, any (m. nom. sg.)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
rapidum: rapidus, -a, -um — snatching, consuming, devouring; swift (m./n. acc. sg.)
rapidus: rapidus, -a, -um — swift, sweeping, ravening (m. nom. sg.)
reductis: redūcō, -ere, -dūxī, -ductum — to draw back (perf. pass. part., m./f./n. abl. pl.)
relinquit: relinquō, -ere, relīquī, relictum — to leave behind, abandon (3rd sg. pres.)
reliquit: relinquō, -ere, relīquī, relictum — to leave behind, abandon (3rd sg. perf.)
remuli: Remulus, -ī (m.) — Remulus, i.e. Numanus Remulus, the Rutulian Ascanius kills (gen. sg.)
respectant: respectō, -āre — to look back at, regard (3rd pl. pres.)
revoluta: revolvō, -ere, -volvī, -volūtum — to roll back, turn back (perf. pass. part., f. nom. sg.; revoluta est, she rolled back)
ripis: rīpa, -ae (f.) — bank of a river (abl./dat. pl.)
ritu: rītus, -ūs (m.) — rite, custom; ritū, after the manner of (abl. sg.)
robore: rōbur, rōboris (n.) — oak; hard timber (abl. sg.)
ruina: ruīna, -ae (f.) — collapse, downfall, ruin (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
ruit: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.)
rumpunt: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, burst, force (3rd pl. pres.)
rutulos: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Rutulians, Turnus's people in Latium (acc. pl.)
sacrum: sacer, sacra, sacrum — sacred, holy (n. acc. sg.) · also m. acc. sg. (sacrum Polyphoetēn) · also n. nom. sg., predicate (tibi sacrum, sacred to you)
saeva: saevus, -a, -um — fierce, savage, cruel (n. acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (Gorgone saevā); n. nom./acc. pl. · also f. nom. sg. (dea saeva)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
secum: sē + cum — with himself/herself/themselves; to oneself
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedibus: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, home; base, foundation (abl./dat. pl.)
sedit: sedeō, -ēre, sēdī, sessum — to sit; to settle, lodge fast (3rd sg. perf.; sīdō has the same perfect)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sinu: sinus, -ūs (m.) — curve, bay, gulf, fold (abl./dat. sg.)
sola: sōlus, -a, -um — alone, only (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sonipes: sonipēs, -pedis (m.) — noisy-footed one; war-horse, steed (nom. sg.)
sonuere: sonō, -āre, -uī, -itum — to sound, resound, clang (3rd pl. perf. = sonuērunt)
spicula: spīculum, -ī (n.) — sharp point, dart, arrowhead (acc. pl.)
spiculaque: spīculum, -ī (n.) — sharp point, dart, arrowhead (acc./nom. pl.) + -que, and
stridente: strīdō, -ere, strīdī — to whir, hiss, creak (pres. part., m./f./n. abl. sg.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
summis: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.; summīs in montibus)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
superbas: superbus, -a, -um — proud, haughty, arrogant (f. acc. pl.)
superis: superus, -a, -um — upper, above; superī (m. pl.), the gods above (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
supplex: supplex, supplicis — suppliant, begging humbly (nom. sg.)
surgit: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, arise (3rd sg. pres.)
suspendit: suspendō, -ere, -pendī, -pensum — to hang up, suspend (3rd sg. pres.)
sustulit: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to raise, lift up (3rd sg. perf.)
tali: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (m./f./n. abl. sg.; n. dat. sg.)
tantus: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. sg.)
tegmine: tegmen, tegminis (n.) — covering, hide, skin (abl. sg.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
telorum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (gen. pl.)
telum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, spear, arrow, weapon (acc./nom. sg.)
tenens: teneō, tenēre, tenuī — to hold (pres. part., nom. sg.)
tereti: teres, teretis — rounded, smooth, polished (f. abl. sg.)
terrent: terreō, -ēre, -uī, -itum — to frighten, terrify (3rd pl. pres.)
tertia: tertius, -a, -um — third (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tertia hastilia)
testor: testor, -ārī, testātus sum — to call to witness, swear by (1st sg. pres., deponent)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
timet: timeō, -ēre, timuī — to fear, be afraid of (3rd sg. pres.)
tollunt: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise; se tollere, to rise up (3rd pl. pres.)
torsit: torqueō, -ēre, torsī, tortum — to twist, turn, hurl (3rd sg. perf.)
tremit: tremō, -ere, -uī — to tremble, quake, shake (3rd sg. pres.)
tristis: tristis, -e — sad, grim, gloomy (m./f. nom. sg.; acc. pl. in -is = -ēs)
triviae: Trivia, -ae (f.) — Trivia, Diana/Hecate, goddess of the crossroads (gen./dat. sg.)
troes: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (nom. pl., Greek form Trōes)
troiana: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
tros: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg. (Tros Anchisiade)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuam: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. acc. sg.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbatae: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to disturb, confuse, enrage (perf. pass. part., f. gen. sg.; also dat. sg., nom. pl.)
turmas: turma, -ae (f.) — troop, squadron, cavalry troop (acc. pl.)
tusci: Tuscus, -a, -um — Tuscan, Etruscan (m. gen. sg., with amnis, the Tiber; also m. nom. pl.)
tyrrhena: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Tyrrhenian, Etruscan (f. abl. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
tyrrhenus: Tyrrhēnus, -ī (m.) — an Etruscan, here Mezentius (nom. sg.); also adj., Etruscan
ubera: ūber, ūberis (n.) — udder, teat, breast (acc./nom. pl.)
umbra: umbra, -ae (f.) — shade, shadow (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
umeri: umerus, -ī (m.) — shoulder (gen. sg.; also nom. pl.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
unam: ūnus, -a, -um — one, one alone, single (f. acc. sg.)
undae: unda, -ae (f.) — wave, water (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
urgetur: urgeō, -ēre, ursī — to press hard, beset, crowd (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
uterque: uterque, utraque, utrumque — each of two, both (m. nom. sg.)
utque: ut (conj.) — that, so that, as, when (+ -que 'and')
vellem: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, be willing (1st sg. impf. subj.)
vellit: vellō, -ere, vellī (vulsī), vulsum — to pluck, tear, wrench away (3rd sg. pres.)
velocem: vēlōx, -ōcis — swift, fleet, quick (m./f. acc. sg.)
venit: veniō, venīre, vēnī — to come (3rd sg. perf. vēnit, or pres. venit)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
vertunt: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, direct, wheel (3rd pl. pres.)
verum: vērum (conj.) — but, but yet (adverbial n. acc. sg. of vērus) · also vērus, -a, -um — true, real (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
vir: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. sg.)
viresque: vīs (f.) — force; pl. vīrēs, strength (acc. pl.) + -que, and
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vocavit: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (3rd sg. perf.)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
volsci: Volscī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Volscians, a people of Latium (nom. pl.)
volvitur: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, tumble (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
volvuntur: volvō, -ere, volvī, volūtum — to roll; pass. roll, flow (3rd pl. pres. pass.)
voveo: voveō, -ēre, vōvī, vōtum — to vow, promise solemnly, dedicate (1st sg. pres.)
